answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work over time, like a reef built coral by coral rather than conjured overnight. New agents start on a low knoll of trust and must complete attested tasks, with peers vouching only after sustained honest behavior. A single operator spinning up thousands of clones cannot fake months of distinct, checkable history, so the rare pearl is an identity whose long record makes its endorsements valuable, while cheap clones stay powerless.
